title: Profiling and Measuring Performance
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Profiling and Measuring Performance in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Profiling and Measuring Performance within Performance and Optimization. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Profiling avoids guesswork and helps developers optimize the bottleneck that users actually experience.

content_blocks.title: Profiling and Measuring Performance: Measure before optimizing
content_blocks.alt_text: Measure before optimizing diagram for lesson 133: Profiling and Measuring Performance. Record the same route, data, and device → Identify the actual render or bundle bottleneck → Repeat measurements and check behavior
content_blocks.caption: Performance workflow: measure a reproducible baseline, optimize the observed bottleneck, and repeat the same test.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Vue performance work starts with measurement and distinguishes initial load costs from reactive update costs. This lesson focuses on Profiling and Measuring Performance. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Vue DevTools profiling
items.text: For Vue DevTools profiling, measure first and optimize the constrained resource rather than guessing. Compare before/after behavior, keep stable identity for rendered lists, and verify that an optimization does not make the code harder to maintain.

items.title: Browser performance tools

items.title: Measuring rendering behavior
items.text: For Measuring rendering behavior, express the intended DOM result through a Vue template binding instead of directly manipulating the DOM. Keep template expressions small, use stable keys for stateful list items, and choose directives based on whether content should be created, removed, or merely hidden.

items.title: Identifying slow interactions
items.text: For Identifying slow interactions, define one source of truth and separate stored state from derived values and actions. Avoid duplicating the same fact in component-local state and a global store; persist only what the product genuinely needs.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Run as App.vue. For very large datasets, measure and consider server filtering or a maintained virtualization component.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Profiling and Measuring Performance with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Browser performance tools”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Vue performance work starts with measurement and distinguishes initial load costs from reactive update costs. For Profiling and Measuring Performance, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Profiling and Measuring Performance” that applies “Vue DevTools profiling”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Vue DevTools profiling”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Profiling and Measuring Performance belongs to the broader area Performance and Optimization.
The main concept to practice is Vue DevTools profiling.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
